overview: Rise 5.99's Speed is a thirty-plus-mode movement module that spreads its logic across five event handlers: onPreMotion is the master tick switch that implements most modes, onMove runs the Mineplex and Verus Low/YPort strafe sequences, onStrafe executes the friction-tuned modes (Cubecraft, Hypixel2/3, NCP Latest, Hypixel) from the client's strafe event, onPacketSend cancels or re-buffers outgoing packets, and onPacketReceive eats or reacts to S08 teleports. The default Custom mode is a full toolkit: jump control, per-tick horizontal strafe pins with randomized jitter, onGround flag spoofing, extra grounded C04 duplicates, fast-fall, void teleports and a timer multiplier. The per-server modes range from near-vanilla bhops (Strafe Hop, Minemenclub Hop) to packet-spam converters (Vulcan2, Convert Ground), timer abuse (Timer Bypass, NCP, Hypixel), and ground-spoofed hops that fly on the vertical axis (Verus Float, Predictive).

sections.p: The module carries a huge settings tower (Custom, Hypixel, NCP Latest, Verus, Timer Bypass and Vape parameter groups) and a handful of state fields: ticks, offGroundTicks, onGroundTicks, stage, startY, speed, jumped, bool, touchedGround, verusEpicBypassBooleanTM, and an ArrayDeque<Packet> used by Timer Bypass. onPreMotion increments ticks and ticksDisable, and everything is gated behind a 50-tick grace period: below 50 the handler returns, at exactly 50 onEnable() re-initializes the state. The module refuses to run while the Fly module is enabled, and onPacketReceive reacts to every S08PacketPlayerPosLook: with disableOnFlag (default on) a teleport sets ticksDisable = 0, calls onDisable() and shows a notification, so the module re-arms after the grace period instead of staying flagged; the Zonecraft mode instead eats the S08 and re-sends the teleport target as a C04 with onGround true, Hypixel2 cancels a single S08, and Vulcan2 cancels any S08 within 10 blocks. onDisable restores speedInAir 0.02, jumpMovementFactor 0.02 and timer 1.0, flushes any buffered packets through sendPacketWithoutEvent, and with Stop on Disable zeroes the motion. The smoothCamera setting hides the hop visually by driving EntityPlayer.enableCameraYOffset and cameraYPosition from startY whenever posY rises above it.

Custom is the mode the user is expected to tune, and each toggle attacks a different server-side envelope. On a ground tick while moving it jumps with customMotionY (the value is snapped to exactly 0.42f when it is within 1.0E-3 of vanilla, so the default jump is indistinguishable from a real one) and pins the horizontal speed with MoveUtil.strafe(customSpeed + randomize), where randomize is a symmetric jitter drawn from randomizeSpeed/100. With Abide Friction enabled the pin is replaced by a momentum-preserving strafe: ground ticks re-apply customSpeed, air ticks call strafe() with the current magnitude so friction decays it naturally. groundDisabler alternates the reported ground flag (event.setGround(ticks % 2 == 0)), Extra OnGround Packets injects up to ten duplicate C04 positions with onGround true per tick, fastFall drops motionY to -customFallMotion on the chosen off-ground tick, VoidTP sends a C04 at posY - 16 - Math.random() every N ticks to keep the server's move window open, and the timer setting (plus timerRandom jitter) multiplies client ticks. groundSpoofMode completes the set with three rewrites of the packet flag: On forces ground true every tick, Air forces it false, and Tick forces it true on a chosen interval.

Timer Bypass is the purest timer exploit in the file: onPacketSend buffers every outgoing packet into the deque, cancels it, runs mc.timer.timerSpeed at the speedTimer setting (2.0 by default), and every pulse ticks (default 20) flushes the whole buffer through sendPacketWithoutEvent, which bypasses the event bus so the re-sent packets are not re-buffered - 40 ticks of movement compressed into a 20-tick burst. Vulcan2 fires five C06/C04 packets per ground tick (midpoint pairs at y - 0.0784, onGround alternating) on top of a 2.5x base strafe. Convert Ground re-emits up to `distance` (2-200) C06 packets every howOften ticks, each spaced speed*(i+1) blocks along the movement vector with randomized yaw and pitch. NCP Latest jumps with 0.4 + rand/500 motion, multiplies ground motionX/Z by speedMultiplierNCP (1.05 default, up to 1.35), raises speedInAir to 0.02-0.06, and its smartTimer computes timerSpeed = 1.337 - current speed (clamped 0.6-1.5). The Hypixel mode low-hops with 0.4/0.42 jumps shaped by lowHopYModification (a lookup keyed to the rounded y-fraction that returns 0.31, 0.04, -0.2 or -0.14 at the canonical hop heights), strafes at baseMoveSpeed * 1.6 on ground (2x on ice), bleeds speed with bunny = (0.84 + rand/50) * (lastDist - base), and runs the timer at hypixelTimer - rand/50. Verus Hop jumps and strafes 0.55/0.349, cancels every C0F in onPacketSend, and spams C0B sneak/sprint every 200ms; Verus Float ground-spoofs with setGround(true) and motionY 0.42 at timer 2.1 on the ground, then holds motionY 0 and timer 0.9 in the air with the ground flag forced true (and the onGround field itself set true), throttling to strafe 0.2865 after ten air ticks.

files.label: Speed.java (module)
files.explanation: The whole module is this file, and the handlers split the work by event type. onPreMotion is the mode switch: it maintains the ground/air tick counters, performs the Custom toolkit, the bhop-family modes (Strafe Hop, Minemenclub Hop, Mineplex Low/Smooth, CraftPlay, KoksCraft, BlocksMC, Taka, Spartan, Zonecraft, Exempted Value, Predictive, Intave, Invadedlands, AAC 4 Simple, Redesky, Vulcan) and the Verus Hop/Float sub-modes. onMove carries the Verus Low/YPort sequences and the Mineplex stage machine (0.42 jump, speed += base/2 capped at 1, 0.985 decay, air strafe at max(base, speed)). onStrafe implements the friction-manipulating modes: Cubecraft sets the ground friction to max(base, speed * 0.91) on the strafe event itself, Hypixel2/3 and Hypixel blend the strafe vector (motionX = (motionX*3 + old)/4) and apply potion multipliers, and NCP Latest runs its speedInAir and smartTimer logic there. onPacketSend is where packets are cancelled: Verus Hop cancels every C0F, Custom cancels C0F (cancelC0F) and C00 (cancelC00), MineBox cancels every C03 on minebox servers, and Timer Bypass re-buffers everything. onPacketReceive handles S08 teleports (disableOnFlag self-disable, Zonecraft eater, Hypixel2 single cancel, Vulcan2 radius cancel) and the S00 disconnect that resets the balance counter.

files.label: MoveUtil.java (strafe math)
files.explanation: MoveUtil (ported from LiquidBounce) is the shared math behind every mode. strafe(speed) writes motionX = -sin(yaw) * speed and motionZ = cos(yaw) * speed using getDirection(), which flips the yaw 180 degrees when moving backward and offsets it 90 * forward per strafe key; strafe() with no argument preserves the current magnitude from getSpeed(). getBaseMoveSpeed returns 0.2873 scaled by 1 + 0.2 * (amplifier + 1) per speed-potion level, and getAllowedHorizontalDistance re-derives NCP's own model (0.221 base, 1.3 sprint factor, potion scaling, 2.5x on ice) so the Hypixel2/3 modes can strafe exactly at the server's allowance. getPredictedMotionY implements (motionY - 0.08) * 0.98 (the gravity step the modes use for their re-jump and fast-fall packets), getJumpMotion adds 0.1 per jump-potion level, and setMoveEvent writes the event delta with the 45-degree diagonal blend so the reported C03 vector matches the motion fields the physics step will consume.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement physics envelope)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly rebuilds the client's physics from the world. In check() the horizontal allowance comes from prepareSpeedEstimation (line 683), which picks friction and acceleration by medium (on-ground friction cubed vs Magic.AIR_ACCELERATION) and feeds estimateNextSpeed to predict the per-tick distance; the vertical allowance comes from vDistRel, and the violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100 with a set-back to the stored location. Critically, fromOnGround and toOnGround come from RichBoundsLocation.isOnGround(), a block ray trace, not the packet's flag, so every ground-spoofing switch in the Custom mode (groundDisabler, groundSpoofMode on/air/tick, the extraGround C04s with onGround true) cannot relax the envelope. The Custom pin at the default 0.35 blocks per tick already exceeds the ~0.28-0.31 sprint prediction, so hdistrel is around 0.04-0.07 and the violation fires on the first move; the Hypixel mode's 1.6x ground strafe (0.4597 bpt), the NCP mode's speedMulti 1.1 re-pin, and Vulcan2's 2.5x base strafe breach it by far more. The 0.42 jump and the 0.4 low hops stay inside the vertical jump envelope (vDistRel accepts jump motion and arms a 10-tick jumpDelay), so the vertical side is clean - the hdistrel tag is the signal.

countering.label: MorePackets (movement packet rate)
countering.explanation: MorePackets counts the raw serverbound move rate, content-blind. Every processed move is scored into data.morePacketsFreq, an ActionFrequency with 500ms buckets, and NetStatic.morePacketsCheck accumulates the window score against cc.morePacketsEPSMax (22/s, 20 ideal) plus a burst path on the newest half-second bucket (default 15 packets, 10 direct-violation). This is the direct hit on the packet-spam modes. Vulcan2 fires five C06/C04 packets per ground tick - roughly 100/s while hopping - so the window accumulator runs at nearly five times the ceiling and the half-second burst path trips on the very first hop. Convert Ground's burst of up to 200 C06 packets in a single tick is a textbook burst violation, and the Custom mode's extraGround (up to 10 C04 per tick) and voidTP C04s pile onto the same counter. Timer Bypass is caught on the flush: the whole deque is re-emitted in one tick, so even though the buffering keeps the *average* rate near normal, the pulse flush is a burst of 40 packets in one half-second bucket. Because the check never inspects positions, none of the module's ground-spoofing or jitter hides the count.

countering.label: Speed (BunnyHop / onGround expected)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's Speed compares thisMove against expectations built from getBaseMoveSpeed (0.2873) plus a stage chosen by vertical speed: 0.049 at zero vertical, 0.08 while descending below 0.34, 0.3261 while still rising. The default Custom speed of 0.35 sits just under the descending expectation of 0.3673, so the mode only evades at its floor value - raising Custom Speed, enabling randomizeSpeed, or switching to a multiplier mode crosses it immediately: the Hypixel 1.6x ground strafe produces 0.4597 on the descending half of every hop, the NCP mode's speedMulti 1.1 re-pin and Vulcan2's 2.5x base do the same, and all of them trip the BunnyHop offground_expected branch with the measured and expected values in the message. The ground branch (expected = thisMove / groundTime + baseMove, groundTime capped at 8, active after 5+ grounded ticks) catches the pinned-speed modes whenever the player stops hopping and runs on the surface, and the onground_block branch (block above + jumping + thisMove > blockMoveMax 0.6699) catches the overdriven hops. Every non-failing move stores the from location as the set-back, so a flagged hop snaps the player back a full tick.

countering.label: Speed (momentum model, discrepancy accumulator)
countering.explanation: Hawk's Speed treats movement as momentum conservation: expected = friction * lastSpeed * handleMultipliers + (maxForce + handleAdders + EPSILON), where friction is the block slipperiness (0.6 on ground, 0.91 in air), maxForce is the maximum input acceleration the move could receive, and sprint-jumping adds a 0.2 adder. The difference between the current speed and expected is a Discrepancy that accumulates across moves, and when the total passes DISCREPANCY_THRESHOLD (0.1) the check punishes with VL = discrepancy * 10 and rubber-bands the player to the server position. Rise's Custom pin works against this model because the expected value is built from the previous move: with ground friction 0.6 and a pinned lastSpeed of 0.35, expected lands near 0.31, so each hop tick contributes a discrepancy of a few hundredths and the accumulator crosses 0.1 within a few hops; at the default 0.35 it takes a handful of hops, and at any higher setting or in the multiplier modes it is immediate. The jump and step exemptions only forgive the vanilla sprint-jump adder, not a magnitude pinned above the friction-reconciled value.
